items.text: Voted to leave public health coverage for older residents intact: the budget law cut none of that coverage's benefits for citizens. In the existing system, public health coverage is guaranteed only to older, disabled, and low-income residents, and about 8 percent of residents have no coverage.
Voted for a budget law that reduced funding for public health coverage for low-income residents, added work requirements to that coverage, and reduced food assistance.
Voted against a three-year extension of expanded premium subsidies for individually purchased health insurance.
Voted for a bill that loosened rules for employer and association health plans and did not extend the expiring premium subsidies.
Voted for a funding bill that did not extend the expiring premium subsidies.
Introduced a bill to replace premium subsidies paid to insurers with personal health accounts that people use to buy their own coverage.

As chair of a group of legislators, released a framework urging the party to pass a bill that makes all non-citizens ineligible for public health coverage for low-income residents, food assistance, and housing assistance, and that ends a dedicated fund for disease prevention.
Called the employer health plan bill a solid first step toward lower costs.
